paper_metadata.title: Microstructure control and mechanical properties from isothermal forging and heat treatment of Ti-22Al-25Nb (at.%) orthorhombic alloy

evidence.quote: The microstructural evolution, creep, and tensile deformation behavior of an orthorhombic Ti-22Al-25Nb (at.%) alloy was investigated by thermo-mechanical processing, including common forging, isothermal forging, and heat treatment.

Ti-22Al-25Nb bar (240 mm diameter, 360 mm length) was provided by Central Iron and Steel Research Institute (CISRI). The chemical analysis as provided in Table 1 shows that the bar composition correlates with the nominal composition, and that the gas impurity content is low (e.g. oxygen ≤ 500 ppm, hydrogen ≤ 300 ppm, and nitrogen ≤ 800 ppm). The microstructure of the Ti-22Al-25Nb bar is shown in Fig. 1a.

Three isothermal forging schedules: 980 °C (HT-1: α2 + B2 + O phase region), 1040 °C (HT-2: α2 + B2 phase region) and 1060 °C (HT-3: B2 phase region) were used to improve the alloy properties. Isothermal forging was carried out at strain rates of 0.05 s−1. The height reduction of the cylindrical cakes was more than 50% in one stroke. The isothermal forged alloys were then machined to form cylinders of 13 mm diameter and 14 mm height for heat treatment. The specimens were solution-treated at 940 °C for 1 h followed by water quenching, and then age-treated at 800 °C for 12 h followed by air cooling to study creep and tensile properties.

Isothermal forging was conducted on a computer-controlled 500 ton hydraulic press with nickel-base super-alloy flat dies, and an electric resistance heating furnace that was sealed in an argon-filled chamber. The cylindrical cakes were heated to the forging temperature with the tools and were soaked for 2 h. After isothermal forging, samples were removed from the dies and cooled in air.
